typed:
Okay, here is where things stand after this week. We spent most of Monday with the stack work team going through the onboarding flow, and the main thing we found is that new users get lost right after they create their first workspace. They see an empty screen with no hint of what to do next, and about a third of them leave before they invite anyone. We sketched three options for fixing it. The first is a short checklist that sits in the corner until they finish it. The second is a sample project that is already filled in, so they can poke around before building their own. The third is a guided tour, but nobody on the call liked that one very much because tours tend to get skipped.

On Tuesday and Wednesday the design team mocked up the first two options. The checklist looked cleaner, but the sample project tested better with the five people we showed it to, mostly because they could see what a finished workspace looks like. We want to try both in an experiment next sprint and measure how many people invite a teammate in their first day. Marketing asked whether we could reuse the sample project in the launch video, which seems fine as long as the data in it is clearly made up.

The other big topic was performance. The dashboard has been slow for larger accounts, and on Thursday we traced most of it to a few queries that load every event instead of a summary. Priya has a fix that adds a daily rollup table, and the first numbers look like the page loads about four times faster for the biggest customers. We still need to decide how far back the rollups go and what happens to accounts that change time zones. There is also a small risk that the rollup job falls behind during the end of month rush, so we will add an alert for that before we turn it on for everyone.

Finally, hosting. We are still planning to move the background jobs off the old servers and onto super base by the end of the quarter. The migration plan is written, and the next step is a dry run on the staging copy next Friday. If that goes well we will move the smaller customers first and keep the old servers running for two weeks in case we need to roll back.
